beliefs.practice: Read the DocumentDB/MongoDB connection string only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime; never hard-code or write it to logs or repo files. Use a .env.example with a placeholder instead of the real URI.

Use a single shared Mongoose connection (singleton) across the app, configured with modern driver options (e.g., useNewUrlParser: true, useUnifiedTopology: true, maxPoolSize appropriate for workload) and close it gracefully on shutdown to avoid connection leaks.
Enable TLS/SSL for the MongoDB connection and do not allow invalid certificates (tls=true, tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false) so credentials and data in transit are encrypted.
Avoid storing monetary amounts as IEEE floats. Store money as integers (cents) or use a fixed-point decimal type (Decimal128) and index that field for amount-based searches.
Create and maintain a compound index on the fields used for candidate matching (e.g., { vendor_normalized: 1, amount: 1 }) so vendor + amount range queries use an index rather than a collection scan.

Store a normalized vendor field (lowercased, trimmed, canonicalized) specifically for equality/case-insensitive matching and index that field instead of relying on case-sensitive free-text vendor names or regex with leading wildcards.

For amount-tolerance searches (amount ± delta), query by a numeric range (amount: { $gte: min, $lte: max }) and ensure amount is indexed; avoid full collection scans by not using application-side filtering after retrieving many documents.

When doing aggregation-heavy scoring (LLM-scored candidates), use server-side aggregation pipelines (limit and project early) and only return fields needed for scoring to reduce network transfer and deserialization costs.

Create vector indexes explicitly on the embedding field with parameters matching your embeddings (dimension, metric) and tune index parameters (HNSW M, efConstruction or IVF params) at creation time to match recall/latency requirements; keep embedding dimension consistent across documents.

Normalize and (if required by index type) L2-normalize embedding vectors at indexing time if the vector index expects normalized vectors; store vector dimension and version in the document schema so changes are detectable.

Use the driver's retryableWrites and retryReads settings and add application-level retry with exponential backoff for transient network errors (socket timeouts, network blips); make retries idempotent or use idempotency keys for non-idempotent writes.

For reconciliations that update multiple documents (invoice flagged matched and PO annotated), use multi-document transactions (startSession + withTransaction) so the set of writes is consistent if the cluster supports MongoDB transactions.

Make seed scripts idempotent: insert or update by a unique business key (upsert) so repeated runs do not create duplicates. Also create indexes idempotently at startup (createIndex is safe to call repeatedly).
Limit returned fields in queries (projection) and use cursor batchSize when scanning candidate sets; avoid loading full documents when only IDs, vendor, amount and embedding are needed for scoring.

Implement server-side verification of any manual corrections submitted through the Express API (validate user input, require authentication/authorization) and record audit metadata (user, timestamp, original value) with the reconciliation result.
Do not store OpenAI API keys or other LLM secrets in the database; read them from environment at runtime and restrict access. Mask or redact any secret values in logs and stack traces.
Avoid expensive regex queries for vendor matching; prefer equality on normalized fields, text indexes, or tokenized fields. If you must use regex, avoid leading wildcards so indexes can be used.

Use explain() and the MCP tools to verify query plans and identify collection scans; add or adjust indexes before running reconciliation at scale and monitor index sizes to control storage and memory footprint.
Use range-based pagination (e.g., last-seen id or sort key) instead of skip/limit for iterative reconciliation over large collections; skip causes increasing server work and poor performance.

Encrypt sensitive fields at rest or use client-side field-level encryption for PII (vendor contact info, bank account numbers) so manual corrections and stored documents do not expose secrets if DB is compromised.
When storing or indexing embeddings, include a timestamp and a schema/version field in each document so you can safely rebuild indexes or re-embed documents if the model or vector schema changes.

Avoid expensive client-side scoring over large candidate sets: prefilter with indexed fields (amount/vendor) to a small candidate set, then run LLM/embedding scoring only on that reduced set to control cost and latency.
Protect the reconciliation API endpoints (Express) with authentication and RBAC; do not accept unauthenticated manual-correction requests that would mutate reconciliation status in the DB.

Monitor connection pool usage, operation latency and index usage and set appropriate serverSelectionTimeoutMS and socketTimeoutMS to detect and recover from connectivity issues to the managed cluster.

When creating vector indexes or changing heavy indexes, do so during maintenance windows and understand RU/IO/CPU impact on the cluster; create indexes in the smallest scope needed (collection) and drop unused indexes.
